title: When the water is full
hook: Stir harder and the last of the salt will go. Will it?

doesNotKnow: that dissolving has a ceiling for a given amount of water and temperature
that at the ceiling dissolving keeps running both ways

misconception: With enough stirring everything dissolves; undissolved salt is just 'not yet'.
objective: The learner can explain that 100 g of water at 20 °C holds about 36 g of salt, so 50 g leaves about 14 g as crystals however long you stir, because at saturation ions leave and rejoin the crystals at the same rate.

claims.text: About 36 g of table salt (NaCl) dissolves in 100 g of water at 20 °C.
claims.source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Aqueous solubility of inorganic compounds': NaCl 26.4 mass % at 20 °C, i.e. 35.9 g per 100 g water; rounded to 36 in Demo.tsx (SOL).

claims.text: Stirring 50 g of salt into 100 g of water at 20 °C leaves about 14 g undissolved.
claims.source: 50 g − 36 g = 14 g (with 35.9 g: 14.1 g). Node script; computed in Demo.tsx as ASK − SOL.

claims.text: More stirring does not dissolve more salt once the water is saturated.
claims.source: Definition of a saturated solution: solid and solution in equilibrium (IUPAC Gold Book, 'saturated solution'; Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles, ch. on solubility). Stirring changes the speed of reaching equilibrium, not the limit.

claims.text: At saturation ions still leave the crystals, and just as many land back on them, so the pile stays the same size.
claims.source: Dynamic equilibrium of dissolution and crystallisation (Atkins & Jones, Chemical Principles; Brown et al., Chemistry: The Central Science, 'saturated solutions and solubility'). The stage's arrows are schematic.

claims.text: A solution in this state is called saturated.
Warmer water holds a little more salt.
claims.source: CRC Handbook: NaCl solubility rises from about 35.7 g/100 g water at 0 °C to about 39 g at 100 °C.

claims.text: Stage: each dot is half a gram of dissolved salt and each cube a gram of crystals; dots are placed by a seeded generator (seed 11, untuned, positions only).
claims.source: Demo.tsx: dots(n, stir) and pile(g). Illustrative scale, not a count of ions.

recall.question: A jar holds 100 g of water at 20 °C with 40 g of salt in it, stirred for an hour. About how much salt is still solid?
recall.why: 100 g of water at 20 °C holds about 36 g; the other 4 g stays solid however long you stir.
